title: Lesson 54: Federated Data: Salesforce Connect, External Objects, and When Not to Use Them
description: What federation is versus replication, how Salesforce Connect surfaces external data through external objects and query pushdown, and the four reasons federation is the wrong choice.

questions.question: What single principle distinguishes federation from replication when the org needs external data?
options: The data is copied into the org and kept aligned by a pipeline
The data stays at the source and the query is pushed to it
The data is cached in the browser after one full download
The data is loaded nightly into a big object for local querying
questions.explanation: Federation leaves the data in place and moves the computation to it: Salesforce sends the query to the source and renders only the matching rows, whereas replication copies the data in and owns keeping the two copies aligned.

questions.question: What does query pushdown do for a federated query?
options: Translates the WHERE, ORDER BY, and LIMIT into the source's query
Downloads the full external table and filters it inside Salesforce
Copies every matching row into Salesforce storage for later reads
Forces the source into a synchronous write-back for the matched rows
questions.explanation: Pushdown translates the filters, ordering, and pagination from a SOQL query and sends them to the external system, so the source runs the query where the data lives and returns only the matching rows over the wire.

questions.question: Which requirement makes federation the wrong choice?
options: Read-only display of a fresh, authoritative balance on a record page
A low-frequency lookup of clean data that must stay in its source region
An AI assistant that must ground on the external data as if native
A high-governance source that regulation forbids copying into Salesforce
questions.explanation: AI and agent features currently operate on native objects and cannot use external objects as a grounding or activation source, so a requirement that a model read external data as native rules federation out. Writes, cross-object joins, and high-volume access are the other disqualifiers.
